title: 多模态大语言模型的技术演进
content_md: # 多模态大语言模型的技术演进：机制、比较与边界 ## 摘要 本文系统梳理了多模态大语言模型在跨模态理解与生成领域的核心进展与挑战。首先，从早期联合嵌入到基于统一分词器的掩码预测，跨模态特征融合实现了向统一语义空间的深度演进。其次，统一架构中不同模态间的容量限制与互相干扰，推动了稀疏混合专家（MoE）与多样化条件掩码及显式匹配策略的发展。最后，本文剖析了多模态模型在面临泛化边界、事实性多模态幻觉约束、深层跨语言零样本迁移缺陷，以及现实环境长程任务中的鲁棒性失衡等局限性，指出了多模态提示与闭环协同在未来演进中的关键作用。 ## 研究问题与技术前史 多模态大语言模型的核心挑战在于如何消除异构模态间的隔阂并实现深层跨模态语义对齐。在早期阶段，跨模态对齐机制主要依赖联合嵌入（Joint Embedding），即通过将视觉与文本等信号投影到同一个连续向量空间来支持特征级别的跨模态检索与联合建模[1][3]。然而，这种粗粒度映射难以有效捕获模态间复杂的结构依赖。随着Transformer的普及，多模态输入的组织与交互方式发生了根本重构。近期的多模态表示框架引入了统一分词器（Tokenizer），将视觉、语音、文本等异构输入离散化为通用且统一的词元序列，并通过联合统一掩码预测任务，强制不同模态特征在完全共享的语义空间中进行映射与对齐[52]。 在具体的自监督对齐策略上，掩码机制的设计经历了从无条件到有条件的演变。基于遮蔽语言和区域建模的方法允许模型以某一模态的完整观察序列作为条件，去推断另一模态中的遮蔽成分。相较于简单的联合随机掩码，这种条件掩码（Conditioned Masking）机制能更有效地捕捉跨模态间的双向上下文模式与细粒度对应关系[4][43]。此外，针对声学与语言等底层分布差异极大的场景，模型通过引入翻译语言建模（TLM）及模态匹配（如语音-文本匹配STM）等显式的辅助损失，进一步消解了特征空间鸿沟[18]。伴随着对齐机制设计的演进，网络架构逐渐分化为两大阵营：双流架构（如LXMERT、ViLBERT）为不同模态保留独立的编码分支以维系特定的模态属性后再做交互，而单流架构（如UNITER）则倾向于将所有模态特征拼接输入单一Transformer模块，以直接学习全局泛化的上下文嵌入[4][28]。值得注意的是，大多数基于鉴别式掩码任务预训练的编码器虽然擅长语义对齐，但由于缺乏解码结构，其在向多模态生成式任务迁移时面临显著的架构鸿沟[43]。 随着跨模态融合的加深，模态表征间的冲突与博弈逐渐显现。研究证实，在统一架构中强行联合预训练多种高资源模态（如语音与文本）会遭遇显著的模态容量限制（Capacity Limitations），导致信号间的相互干扰，甚至引发特定模态下游性能的退化[18]。为突破这一网络瓶颈，多模态预训练引入了稀疏混合专家（MoE）路由机制。通过优化 top-k 路由策略并设计专家原型（Expert Prototyping）配合 top-1 路由，模型在训练阶段大幅增加了可用参数规模，同时在部署与推理阶段维持了恒定的计算成本。这一策略有效缓解了跨模态表征干扰，并在万亿级别参数的图文联合预训练中展现出了显著的收敛加速能力[15]。 除了模型架构限制，跨模态对齐效果还受制于多模态数据固有的物理特性。图像-文本对齐通常只需关注空间对象与词汇间的静态语义一致性，而涉及视频、音频等连续模态时，则需建立额外的时间维度与节奏对应机制[53]。进一步地，仅依赖静态视听数据集进行的对齐被证明难以实现模型对物理世界的真正理解。为弥合语言系统与真实物理环境间的认知鸿沟，研究指出通过引入具身多模态代理（Embodied Agents），将空间位置、手势姿态等动态情境变量叠加到多模态交互通道中，正成为推动模型跨越表层特征映射、实现深度实体接地（Grounded Understanding）与意图对齐的关键演进方向[11]。 ## 跨模态表示与对齐 跨模态表示与对齐致力于打破独立模态的壁垒。早期的双流模型虽在检索上表现出色，但其对比学习目标容易引发依赖数据增强的采样偏差，且受限的文本编码器难以胜任多模态生成任务[36][44]。为克服这些局限，近期研究在统一架构与融合机制上衍生出多条演进路线。 在统一编码与掩码建模方面，为消除特定模态隔离，M3AE放弃了对比学习，在共享编码器上采用高文本掩码率（50%-90%）的联合掩码标记预测，有效利用了非成对数据[44]。VL-BEiT利用混合模态专家（MoE）Transformer，将掩码图像、掩码语言及跨模态掩码建模在单一主干上统一[51]。面对非对齐海量语料，UNIMO结合跨模态对比学习与文本重写生成的困难负样本来增强语义空间[7]；其演进版本UNIMO-2则构建了共享的视觉-语言基础空间，实现了非对齐图像和文本的端到端联合学习[49]。针对语言与视觉的扩展瓶颈，PaLI模型验证了编码器-解码器语言模型（mT5）与视觉大模型（ViT）联合缩放的可行性[45]。为降低计算负担，Dynamic MDETR在视觉定位解码器中采用2D自适应采样，仅使用少量特征点即可完成文本引导解码[35]；而LXMERT-S则提出基于词、短语到句子粒度的多阶段策略，以极小参数量逼近大模型性能[16]。 将跨模态对齐扩展至多语言环境带来了参数膨胀和语义偏差挑战。MULE采用单一共享语言分支替代独立特定语言模型，有效控制了规模[2]；SMALR进一步提出固定大小的语言无关表示及掩码跨语言建模损失，在极低参数下支持十余种语言[6]。为实现零样本跨语言迁移，UC2等模型通过机器翻译扩充数据，并构建以图像为枢纽的掩码区域建模与翻译建模任务[8][22]。然而机器翻译易丢失文化特征，KELIP通过真实韩英双语图文对和多裁剪增强，成功捕捉到跨语言同义词在视觉语义上的文化差异[40]。为降低语言扩展门槛，MLA框架向单语CLIP中注入轻量级语言获取模块，通过两阶段训练实现低成本扩展[37]。在语音领域，mSLAM将w2v-BERT与SpanBERT结合，通过对齐语音和转录文本的CTC损失，在多语种中建立了跨模态共享表示[58]。针对跨语言VQA，结合语言学先验损失与代码混合增强能显著缓解对源语言的过拟合[39]。 在信息注入与细粒度融合方面，部分研究侧重非破坏性的映射或前缀机制。VaLM通过检索相关图像并在视觉知识融合层中执行注意力计算，直接增强了自回归语言模型[54]；部分研究利用对象感知网络将图像转译为输入空间中的辅助文本序列，在不修改BERT架构的情况下实现了多模态情感分类[13]；另有工作将包含物理感觉运动规范的视觉基础词向量直接替换至ELECTRA等模型中以提供具身物理感知[12]。TEASEL利用语音提取的动态前缀作为预训练语言模型交叉注意力的输入[20]，而HVPNeT将对象级图像特征作为可插拔视觉前缀逐层引导文本，避免了无关图像的干扰[38]。解耦实验证实，模态间相互参考的多模态注意力在零样本检索中优于单模态独立注意力[10]。针对复杂的视频序列，VLM采用掩码模态模型强制网络利用另一模态恢复被遮盖模态，增强了跨模态表示紧密度[24]；VICTOR引入对比代理任务捕捉长视频特有的时空与序列关系[23]；DeCEMBERT则利用熵最小化约束注意力，迫使模型在噪声指令视频中自动聚焦对齐的字幕[9]。 ## 训练数据和交互生成 多模态大语言模型在训练数据利用与交互生成机制上，已从单一范式演进为零样本模型组合与检索增强多模态预训练两大核心分支。 在交互生成方面，无需额外微调的零样本多模型组合机制成为扩展跨模态能力的重要路径。Socratic Models通过多模态提示（Multimodal-informed prompting）引导不同领域分布的预训练模型（如视觉语言模型和纯大语言模型）进行基于语言的零样本信息交换以实现联合推理[48]。然而，这种级联架构存在单向通信局限，后续处理的信息无法回传纠错。为此，迭代共识机制突破了该限制，引入闭环通信优化：由生成器构建初始候选方案，并由多个评分器组成的集成模块提供迭代反馈；这种闭环机制促使模型间相互修正误差，从而提升零样本任务的稳健性[32]。在交互指令形式的拓展上，VIMA架构将跨模态生成目标延伸至具身智能，其将复杂的任务规范统一表达为交织文本与视觉特征序列的多模态提示（Multimodal prompts），并在解码端通过Transformer自回归地输出连续运动控制动作[50]。 在训练数据与知识注入机制方面，为突破静态模型参数对世界知识存储的容量瓶颈，检索增强架构被实质性地引入多模态语言建模中。MuRAG构建了多模态检索增强Transformer，通过联合对比损失与生成损失（Joint contrastive and generative loss），在海量图文及纯文本混合语料上进行预训练，使生成过程能实时访问外部非参数化多模态记忆以完成复杂推理问答[42]。相比之下，RA-CM3进一步实现了检索内容与生成目标的模态对等化。该机制结合了CM3生成器架构与基于CLIP的检索器，不仅在训练时仅需极低的计算开销，更首次具备了检索并直接生成图文混合序列（Mixtures of text and images）的能力，同时解锁了多模态上下文学习的新特性[59]。 针对多模态表征融合的预训练框架层，i-Code超越了传统依赖成对视频数据的对齐范式，提出一种高灵活度的自监督学习机制。该系统前端复用独立预训练的单模态编码器，后端接入多模态融合网络，通过创新的掩码模态单元建模（Masked modality unit modeling）和跨模态对比学习目标进行端到端预训练，使得模型在推理阶段能够动态兼容单、双或三模态数据的任意输入组合[57]。 ## 模态泛化、幻觉与边界 多模态大语言模型在跨模态泛化与生成质量控制上展现出明确的机制分化，其核心研究重点已从基础特征的对齐拼接，直接演进为统一语义空间的离散化映射边界及解码期的事实性约束。 在模态泛化机制的分支演进中，将非结构化、连续的多模态信号强制映射至离散的文本词元空间，已成为实现架构泛化的终局方案，有效规避了早期复杂的跨模态注意力融合设计。例如，MAnTiS方法通过模态特定编码器，将图像与文本直接投影至标准的文本词元空间并构建联合条件前缀；该机制直接引导预训练语言模型生成，无需复杂网络缝合即可实现单模态向多模态的条件生成泛化[17]。面对包含视频与音频的复杂连续流，VX2TEXT框架采用了更彻底的映射策略：引入可学习的连续输入松弛机制（Differentiable Tokenizer），将视频或语音转化为统一的语言嵌入。这种将多模态强制折叠进语言语义空间的操作，使得自回归解码器能够无缝接管多模态特征，彻底消除了针对字幕生成或问答定制专用网络头的需求，实现了判别与生成任务的统一泛化[25]。 然而，高度统一的词元化泛化机制直接暴露出多模态生成的边界——事实性偏移与多模态幻觉。当模型具备强生成自由度时，常输出与条件输入相悖或脱节的细节。针对此局限，干预解码过程成为了更具确定性的机制分支。XFBoost框架放弃对内部注意力权重的隐式干预，转而在解码阶段直接将提取的视觉语义属性注入为显式约束条件。配合策略梯度（Policy Gradient）技术进行强化微调，该机制在不损失生成多样性的前提下，精准压制了违背事实或特征矛盾的幻觉表达，大幅拉升了图文一致性边界[56]。 此外，多模态泛化的极限不仅受制于网络架构，更受到文化与先验分布的严格限制。即使在数据增广和表征解偏的加持下，模态知识的跨领域迁移依然存在物理与文化鸿沟。在多模态机器翻译中，利用预训练视觉语言模型（VLM）虽能缓解平行语料瓶颈，但其实验证据表明多模态对齐存在刚性的文化距离边界。当视觉融合机制应用于与预训练数据（如LXMERT）文化背景差异巨大的目标语言体系时，多模态特征带来的性能增益可能会发生衰退[46]。这表明，多模态大模型的泛化边界无法单靠底层词元映射来无限延伸，物理世界的分布差异构成了当前对齐机制的刚性壁垒。 ## 实验证据与方法比较 多模态模型的评估正经历从单模态、高资源向多语言、多模态全景拓展的演进。为解决多模态任务多语言支持匮乏的问题，GEM基准整合了图像与视频维度的多语言评测，并引入M3P等架构作为统一对照[14]。然而，直接将机器翻译用于构建多语言集往往引入文本伪影，为此Crossmodal-3600要求双语者依据图像生成36种语言的原生描述，建立了规避翻译伪影的高质量参照系[33]。Bloom Library则进一步将基准覆盖面扩展至300多种语言，为极低资源语种确立了零样本评测基线[30]。在模态复杂度的扩展上，MUGEN基准利用强化学习智能体生成带有音频属性的闭世界受控视频，并设计了针对真实样本校准的人类评估协议[41]；CMU-MOSEAS构建了覆盖法语、德语、西班牙语和葡萄牙语的音视频基准，并利用F1分数评估不平衡类别下的多模态情感属性[5]。 为了准确剥离模型的统计拟合捷径，评估机制逐渐向引入严格去偏见对照条件的探针网络发展。传统测试常受语言共现偏置污染，近期的研究通过构建针对性探针来测试视觉概念的真实落地。例如，通过对齐结构以控制目标与干扰项的相互翻转，能有效排查纯语言先验，从而测试模型对谓词-名词的真实跨模态依赖[34]。此外，为消除巨型模型引入的控制变量困难，有研究通过构建“数学-语言”微型沙盒作为对照环境，以低算力开销验证了单流架构在融合机制中优于双流架构的特性，且该结论与视觉语言域的演进结论保持一致[31]。 在更精细的对照条件下，实验发掘出多模态预训练在能力边界和表征习得上的诸多冲突结果。首先，在零样本跨语言评估中，尽管引入架构适配，多模态模型仍会出现约38个准确率分数的骤降，暴露了深层潜在的跨语言多模态严重未对齐[27]。其次，关于模型视觉常识来源的探查得出了反直觉的结论：基于“记忆颜色”探针任务的对照显示，多模态模型表现出的视觉常识水平，纯单模态语言基线仅通过文本预训练即可达到同等水准，多模态预训练在此处并未展现显著增益[55]。在进一步严格过滤文本数据中视觉相关词汇后，纯语言模型依然能表现出部分视觉常识，这暗示模型机制上可能通过二阶同义词泄露来获取跨模态特征[21]。最后，针对颜色与尺寸的多模态探针实验明确证实，模型在处理空间位置和大小推断时仍严重依赖语言先验线索，且针对多模态下游任务的微调操作，并不必然能够改善模型底层的细粒度多模态表征能力[29]。 ## 局限、效率与开放问题 现有多模态大语言模型在理论上追求跨模态信息的平衡整合，但在实际机制中却存在深层的对齐不对称问题。通过非侵入式的跨模态输入消融诊断发现，无论单流还是双流视觉-语言模型，均表现出“视觉辅助语言”而非真正对称的融合模式：完全或选择性地屏蔽视觉输入会大幅增加掩码文本预测的相对困难，而屏蔽文本输入对视觉对象类别（掩码图像区域）的预测几乎不产生任何负面影响[26]。这种现象违背了跨模态双向激活的预设假设。造成此种表征失效的部分原因在于，传统模型依赖外部视觉组件提取的噪声银标准目标分布缺乏可靠性，从而阻碍了语言特征反向指导视觉理解的通道[26]。这表明现有的跨模态架构尚未在深层语义网络中实现各模态地位的完全平等。 在模型向复杂真实世界部署的过程中，物理环境和数据传输产生的分布偏移构成了主要应用限制。针对视频-语言模型的评估显示，跨模态检索系统对于多模态扰动展现出明显的不平衡：模型对文本层面的扰动具有相对较强的鲁棒性，但对视觉层面的扰动（如光照剧变、相机移动或数字压缩）更为敏感且易发生性能退化[47]。在注意力机制分配上，模型倾向于将权重集中于静态场景和物理实体，而对时序运动与具体动作特征的捕捉存在系统性不足[47]。尽管采用预训练范式的模型在应对这些扰动时相较于从头训练的模型表现出更宽的鲁棒性边界，但核心的动作理解缺陷仍是目前视频与语言对齐的未决难题[47]。 针对上述跨模态特征的局限性，部分研究尝试在特定下游应用中引入强化机制。例如，在情感分析等需要细粒度模态交互的任务中，采用独立的自监督学习模型为各单一模态提取高层特征表示，并引入鲁棒的跨模态注意力网络进行融合集成，能够在不依赖严格时间对齐假设的情况下，有效捕捉长程依赖并克服低级特征表征能力薄弱的问题[19]。然而，从整体多模态范式来看，此类方法级别的补救尚未解决宏观验证条件的缺失。真实世界鲁棒性分析常因获取真实分布偏移数据的极高难度，不得不妥协于使用人工模拟噪声进行基准测试[47]。此外，多模态模型的训练和测试严重依赖庞大的GPU算力开销，且基准验证受制于重度预处理要求及模型权重的公开状态，这些工程与资源壁垒直接限制了模型评测的覆盖广度与开放问题的探索进度[47]。 ## 结论 多模态大模型的发展必须突破单纯依靠数据堆砌和底层词元映射的瓶颈。虽然目前的检索增强、零样本模型组合与统一架构机制在多模态生成任务上取得了重要突破，但跨模态间的深层语义不对称、物理特性的内在差异以及不可忽视的刚性文化偏移等问题依旧严峻。基准测试的扩展和严谨的探针实验证实了脱离真实世界验证环境的潜在危险。未来研究亟需探索更为平等的双向跨模态机制，并在架构中更深层次地引入具身物理感知与闭环交互，方能实现模型向深度实体接地和稳健多模态生成的终局进化。 ## source_intervals.text: Multimodal Neural Language Models We introduce two multimodal neural language models: models of natural language that can be conditioned on other modalities. An image-text multimodal neural language model can be used to retrieve images given complex sentence queries, retrieve phrase descriptions given image queries, as well as generate text conditioned on images. We show that in the case of image-text modelling we can jointly learn word representations and image features by training our models together with a convolutional network. Unlike many of the existing methods, our approach can generate sentence descriptions for images without the use of templates, structured prediction, and/or syntactic trees. While we focus on imagetext modelling, our algorithms can be easily applied to other modalities such as audio.

source_intervals.text: MULE: Multimodal Universal Language Embedding Existing vision-language methods typically support two languages at a time at most. In this paper, we present a modular approach which can easily be incorporated into existing vision-language methods in order to support many languages. We accomplish this by learning a single shared Multimodal Universal Language Embedding (MULE) which has been visually-semantically aligned across all languages. Then we learn to relate the MULE to visual data as if it were a single language. Our method is not architecture specific, unlike prior work which typically learned separate branches for each language, enabling our approach to easily be adapted to many vision-language methods and tasks. Since MULE learns a single language branch in the multimodal model, we can also scale to support many languages, and languages with fewer annotations to take advantage of the good representation learned from other (more abundant) language data. We demonstrate the effectiveness of our embeddings on the bidirectional image-sentence retrieval task, supporting up to four languages in a single model. However, many applications in artificial intelligence involve more than one modality. It is therefore of broad interest to study the more difficult and complex problem of modeling and learning across multiple modalities. In this paper, a technical review of the models and learning methods for multimodal intelligence is provided. The main focus is the combination of vision and natural language, which has become an important area in both computer vision and natural language processing research communities. This review provides a comprehensive analysis of recent work on multimodal deep learning from three new angles - learning multimodal representations, the fusion of multimodal signals at various levels, and multimodal applications. On multimodal representation learning, we review the key concept of embedding, which unifies the multimodal signals into the same vector space and thus enables cross-modality signal processing. source_intervals.text: UNITER: Learning UNiversal Image-TExt Representations Joint image-text embedding is the bedrock for most Vision-and-Language (V+L) tasks, where multimodality inputs are jointly processed for visual and textual understanding. In this paper, we introduce UNITER, a UNiversal Image-TExt Representation, learned through large-scale pre-training over four image-text datasets (COCO, Visual Genome, Conceptual Captions, and SBU Captions), which can power heterogeneous downstream V+L tasks with joint multimodal embeddings. We design three pre-training tasks: Masked Language Modeling (MLM), Image-Text Matching (ITM), and Masked Region Modeling (MRM, with three variants). Different from concurrent work on multimodal pre-training that apply joint random masking to both modalities, we use conditioned masking on pre-training tasks (i.e., masked language/region modeling is conditioned on full observation of image/text). Comprehensive analysis shows that conditioned masking yields better performance than unconditioned masking. We also conduct a thorough ablation study to find an optimal setting for the combination of pre-training tasks. While languages such as English have relatively large multimodal language resources, other widely spoken languages across the globe have few or no large-scale datasets in this area. As a step towards building more equitable and inclusive multimodal systems, we introduce the first large-scale multimodal language dataset for Spanish, Portuguese, German and French. The proposed dataset, called CMU-MOSEAS (CMU Multimodal Opinion Sentiment, Emotions and Attributes), is the largest of its kind with 40, 000 total labelled sentences. It covers a diverse set topics and speakers, and carries supervision of 20 labels including sentiment (and subjectivity), emotions, and attributes. Our evaluations on a state-of-the-art multimodal model demonstrates that CMU-MOSEAS enables further research for multilingual studies in multimodal language. source_intervals.text: Learning to Scale Multilingual Representations for Vision-Language Tasks Current multilingual vision-language models either require a large number of additional parameters for each supported language, or suffer performance degradation as languages are added. In this paper, we propose a Scalable Multilingual Aligned Language Representation (SMALR) that represents many languages with few model parameters without sacrificing downstream task performance. SMALR learns a fixed size language-agnostic representation for most words in a multilingual vocabulary, keeping language-specific features for few. We use a novel masked cross-language modeling loss to align features with context from other languages. Additionally, we propose a cross-lingual consistency module that ensures predictions made for a query and its machine translation are comparable. The effectiveness of SMALR is demonstrated with ten diverse languages, over twice the number supported in vision-language tasks to date. We evaluate on multilingual image-sentence retrieval and outperform prior work by 3-4% with less than 1/5th the training parameters compared to other word embedding methods. source_intervals.text: DeCEMBERT: Learning from Noisy Instructional Videos via Dense Captions and Entropy Minimization Leveraging large-scale unlabeled web videos such as instructional videos for pre-training followed by task-specific finetuning has become the de facto approach for many video-and-language tasks. However, these instructional videos are very noisy, the accompanying ASR narrations are often incomplete, and can be irrelevant to or temporally misaligned with the visual content, limiting the performance of the models trained on such data. To address these issues, we propose an improved video-and-language pre-training method that first adds automatically-extracted dense region captions from the video frames as auxiliary text input, to provide informative visual cues for learning better video and language associations. Second, to alleviate the temporal misalignment issue, our method incorporates an entropy minimization-based constrained attention loss, to encourage the model to automatically focus on the correct caption from a pool of candidate ASR captions. Our overall approach is named DeCEMBERT (Dense Captions and Entropy Minimization). Comprehensive experiments on three video-and-language tasks (text-to-video retrieval, video captioning, and video question answering) across five datasets demonstrate that our approach outperforms previous state-of-the-art methods. source_intervals.text: Decoupling the Role of Data, Attention, and Losses in Multimodal Transformers Recently multimodal transformer models have gained popularity because their performance on language and vision tasks suggest they learn rich visual-linguistic representations. source_intervals.text: Embodied Multimodal Agents to Bridge the Understanding Gap In this paper we argue that embodied multimodal agents, i.e., avatars, can play an important role in moving natural language processing toward “deep understanding.” Fully-featured interactive agents, model encounters between two “people,” but a language-only agent has little environmental and situational awareness. Multimodal agents bring new opportunities for interpreting visuals, locational information, gestures, etc., which are more axes along which to communicate. We propose that multimodal agents, by facilitating an embodied form of human-computer interaction, provide additional structure that can be used to train models that move NLP systems closer to genuine “understanding” of grounded language, and we discuss ongoing studies using existing systems. To enrich language models with some of this missing experience, we leverage two sources of information: (1) the Lancaster Sensorimotor norms, which provide ratings (means and standard deviations) for over 40,000 English words along several dimensions of embodiment, and which capture the extent to which something is experienced across 11 different sensory modalities, and (2) vectors from coefficients of binary classifiers trained on images for the BERT vocabulary. We pre-trained the ELECTRA model and fine-tuned the RoBERTa model with these two sources of information then evaluate using the established GLUE benchmark and the Visual Dialog benchmark. We find that enriching language models with the Lancaster norms and image vectors improves results in both tasks, with some implications for robust language models that capture holistic linguistic meaning in a language learning context. The goal of the task is to combine vision and language to understand the sentiment towards a target entity in a sentence. Twitter is an ideal setting for the task because it is inherently multimodal, highly emotional, and affects real world events. However, multimodal tweets are short and accompanied by complex, possibly irrelevant images. source_intervals.text: Multimodal Conditionality for Natural Language Generation Large scale pretrained language models have demonstrated state-of-the-art performance in language understanding tasks. Their application has recently expanded into multimodality learning, leading to improved representations combining vision and language. However, progress in adapting language models towards conditional Natural Language Generation (NLG) has been limited to a single modality, generally text. We propose MAnTiS, Multimodal Adaptation for Text Synthesis, a general approach for multimodal conditionality in transformer-based NLG models. source_intervals.text: VX2TEXT: End-to-End Learning of Video-Based Text Generation From Multimodal Inputs We present \textsc{Vx2Text}, a framework for text generation from multimodal inputs consisting of video plus text, speech, or audio. In order to leverage transformer networks, which have been shown to be effective at modeling language, each modality is first converted into a set of language embeddings by a learnable tokenizer. This allows our approach to perform multimodal fusion in the language space, thus eliminating the need for ad-hoc cross-modal fusion modules. We propose a diagnostic method based on cross-modal input ablation to assess the extent to which these models actually integrate cross-modal information. Model performance is measured by modality-specific tasks that mirror the model pretraining objectives (e.g. masked language modelling for text). source_intervals.text: xGQA: Cross-Lingual Visual Question Answering Recent advances in multimodal vision and language modeling have predominantly focused on the English language, mostly due to the lack of multilingual multimodal datasets to steer modeling efforts. In this work, we address this gap and provide xGQA, a new multilingual evaluation benchmark for the visual question answering task. We extend the established English GQA dataset to 7 typologically diverse languages, enabling us to detect and explore crucial challenges in cross-lingual visual question answering. We further propose new adapter-based approaches to adapt multimodal transformer-based models to become multilingual, and—vice versa—multilingual models to become multimodal. Our proposed methods outperform current state-of-the-art multilingual multimodal models (e.g., M3P) in zero-shot cross-lingual settings, but the accuracy remains low across the board; a performance drop of around 38 accuracy points in target languages showcases the difficulty of zero-shot cross-lingual transfer for this task. source_intervals.text: Composing Ensembles of Pre-trained Models via Iterative Consensus Large pre-trained models exhibit distinct and complementary capabilities dependent on the data they are trained on. Language models such as GPT-3 are capable of textual reasoning but cannot understand visual information, while vision models such as DALL-E can generate photorealistic photos but fail to understand complex language descriptions. In this work, we propose a unified framework for composing ensembles of different pre-trained models -- combining the strengths of each individual model to solve various multimodal problems in a zero-shot manner. We use pre-trained models as"generators"or"scorers"and compose them via closed-loop iterative consensus optimization. The generator constructs proposals and the scorers iteratively provide feedback to refine the generated result. Such closed-loop communication enables models to correct errors caused by other models, significantly boosting performance on downstream tasks, e.g. improving accuracy on grade school math problems by 7.5%, without requiring any model finetuning. For vision-language data, the dominant approaches are based on contrastive learning objectives that train a separate encoder for each modality. While effective, contrastive learning approaches introduce sampling bias depending on the data augmentations used, which can degrade performance on downstream tasks. Moreover, these methods are limited to paired image-text data, and cannot leverage widely-available unpaired data. We provide an empirical study of M3AE trained on a large-scale image-text dataset, and find that M3AE is able to learn generalizable representations that transfer well to downstream tasks. source_intervals.text: VATLM: Visual-Audio-Text Pre-Training with Unified Masked Prediction for Speech Representation Learning Although speech is a simple and effective way for humans to communicate with the outside world, a more realistic speech interaction contains multimodal information, e.g., vision, text. How to design a unified framework to integrate different modal information and leverage different resources (e.g., visual-audio pairs, audio-text pairs, unlabeled speech, and unlabeled text) to facilitate speech representation learning was not well explored. In this paper, we propose a unified cross-modal representation learning framework VATLM (Visual-Audio-Text Language Model). The proposed VATLM employs a unified backbone network to model the modality-independent information and utilizes three simple modality-dependent modules to preprocess visual, speech, and text inputs. In order to integrate these three modalities into one shared semantic space, VATLM is optimized with a masked prediction task of unified tokens, given by our proposed unified tokenizer. We evaluate the pre-trained VATLM on audio-visual related downstream tasks, including audio-visual speech recognition (AVSR), visual speech recognition (VSR) tasks. Results show that the proposed VATLM outperforms previous the state-of-the-art models, such as audio-visual pre-trained AV-HuBERT model, and analysis also demonstrates that VATL

o improve the performance of tasks with different modalities using data from a single modality. VI. CONCLUSION In this paper, we present VATLM, a visual-audio-text self-supervised speech representation

learning model, which achieves competitive even state-of-the-art performance on audio-visual/visual speech recognition tasks. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first work to integrate both visual information and textual information into speech representation learning in a unified framework. We tokenize the data sources from different modalities into shared hidden units, and employ a multipath Transformer to model the latent representation of visual, speech, and text. Particularly, the model is optimized by learning to predict the hidden units of different modalities with a unified masked prediction task. For future work, we are planning to extend to more downstream tasks and model a rich variety of videos with the proposed VATLM. We are also interested in integrating masked autoencoder methods into our model.

source_intervals.text: Vision+X: A Survey on Multimodal Learning in the Light of Data We are perceiving and communicating with the world in a multisensory manner, where different information sources are sophisticatedly processed and interpreted by separate parts of the human brain to constitute a complex, yet harmonious and unified sensing system. To endow the machines with true intelligence, the multimodal machine learning that incorporates data from various modalities has become an increasingly popular research area with emerging technical advances in recent years. In this paper, we present a survey on multimodal machine learning from a novel perspective considering not only the purely technical aspects but also the nature of different data modalities. We analyze the commonness and uniqueness of each data format ranging from vision, audio, text and others, and then present the technical development categorized by the combination of Vision+X, where the vision data play a fundamental role in most multimodal learning works. beats. source_intervals.text: Visually-Augmented Language Modeling Human language is grounded on multimodal knowledge including visual knowledge like colors, sizes, and shapes. However, current large-scale pre-trained language models rely on the text-only self-supervised training with massive text data, which precludes them from utilizing relevant visual information when necessary. To address this, we propose a novel pre-training framework, named VaLM, to Visually-augment text tokens with retrieved relevant images for Language Modeling. Specifically, VaLM builds on a novel text-vision alignment method via an image retrieval module to fetch corresponding images given a textual context. With the visually-augmented context, VaLM uses a visual knowledge fusion layer to enable multimodal grounded language modeling by attending on both text context and visual knowledge in images. We evaluate the proposed model on various multimodal commonsense reasoning tasks, which require visual information to excel. VaLM outperforms the text-only baseline with substantial gains of +8.66% and +37.81% accuracy on object color and size reasoning, respectively. source_intervals.text: XFBoost: Improving Text Generation with Controllable Decoders Multimodal conditionality in transformer-based natural language models has demonstrated state-of-the-art performance in the task of product description generation. Recent approaches condition a language model on one or more images and other textual metadata to achieve near-human performance for describing products from e-commerce stores. However, generated descriptions may exhibit degrees of inaccuracy or even contradictory claims relative to the inputs of a given product. In this paper, we propose a controllable language generation framework called Extract-Finetune-Boost (XFBoost), which addresses the problem of inaccurate low-quality inference. By using visual semantic attributes as constraints at the decoding stage of the generation process and finetuning the language model with policy gradient techniques, the XFBoost framework is found to produce significantly more descriptive text with higher image relevancy, outperforming baselines and lowering the frequency of factually inaccurate descriptions. source_intervals.text: i-Code: An Integrative and Composable Multimodal Learning Framework Human intelligence is multimodal; we integrate visual, linguistic, and acoustic signals to maintain a holistic worldview. Most current pretraining methods, however, are limited to one or two modalities. We present i-Code, a self-supervised pretraining framework where users may flexibly combine the modalities of vision, speech, and language into unified and general-purpose vector representations. In this framework, data from each modality are first given to pretrained single-modality encoders. The encoder outputs are then integrated with a multimodal fusion network, which uses novel attention mechanisms and other architectural innovations to effectively combine information from the different modalities. The entire system is pretrained end-to-end with new objectives including masked modality unit modeling and cross-modality contrastive learning. source_intervals.text: mSLAM: Massively multilingual joint pre-training for speech and text We present mSLAM, a multilingual Speech and LAnguage Model that learns cross-lingual cross-modal representations of speech and text by pre-training jointly on large amounts of unlabeled speech and text in multiple languages. mSLAM combines w2v-BERT pre-training on speech with SpanBERT pre-training on character-level text, along with Connectionist Temporal Classification (CTC) losses on paired speech and transcript data, to learn a single model capable of learning from and representing both speech and text signals in a shared representation space. We evaluate mSLAM on several downstream speech understanding tasks and find that joint pre-training with text improves quality on speech translation, speech intent classification and speech language-ID while being competitive on multilingual ASR, when compared against speech-only pre-training. Our speech translation model demonstrates zero-shot text translation without seeing any text translation data, providing evidence for cross-modal alignment of representations. mSLAM also benefits from multi-modal fine-tuning, further improving the quality of speech translation by directly leveraging text translation data during the fine-tuning process. source_intervals.text: Retrieval-Augmented Multimodal Language Modeling Recent multimodal models such as DALL-E and CM3 have achieved remarkable progress in text-to-image and image-to-text generation. However, these models store all learned knowledge (e.g., the appearance of the Eiffel Tower) in the model parameters, requiring increasingly larger models and training data to capture more knowledge. To integrate knowledge in a more scalable and modular way, we propose a retrieval-augmented multimodal model, which enables a base multimodal model (generator) to refer to relevant knowledge fetched by a retriever from external memory (e.g., multimodal documents on the web). Specifically, we implement a retriever using the pretrained CLIP model and a generator using the CM3 Transformer architecture, and train this model using the LAION dataset. sections.title: 研究问题与技术前史
sections.body:
多模态大语言模型的核心挑战在于如何消除异构模态间的隔阂并实现深层跨模态语义对齐。在早期阶段，跨模态对齐机制主要依赖联合嵌入（Joint Embedding），即通过将视觉与文本等信号投影到同一个连续向量空间来支持特征级别的跨模态检索与联合建模[1][3]。然而，这种粗粒度映射难以有效捕获模态间复杂的结构依赖。随着Transformer的普及，多模态输入的组织与交互方式发生了根本重构。近期的多模态表示框架引入了统一分词器（Tokenizer），将视觉、语音、文本等异构输入离散化为通用且统一的词元序列，并通过联合统一掩码预测任务，强制不同模态特征在完全共享的语义空间中进行映射与对齐[52]。

在具体的自监督对齐策略上，掩码机制的设计经历了从无条件到有条件的演变。基于遮蔽语言和区域建模的方法允许模型以某一模态的完整观察序列作为条件，去推断另一模态中的遮蔽成分。相较于简单的联合随机掩码，这种条件掩码（Conditioned Masking）机制能更有效地捕捉跨模态间的双向上下文模式与细粒度对应关系[4][43]。此外，针对声学与语言等底层分布差异极大的场景，模型通过引入翻译语言建模（TLM）及模态匹配（如语音-文本匹配STM）等显式的辅助损失，进一步消解了特征空间鸿沟[18]。伴随着对齐机制设计的演进，网络架构逐渐分化为两大阵营：双流架构（如LXMERT、ViLBERT）为不同模态保留独立的编码分支以维系特定的模态属性后再做交互，而单流架构（如UNITER）则倾向于将所有模态特征拼接输入单一Transformer模块，以直接学习全局泛化的上下文嵌入[4][28]。值得注意的是，大多数基于鉴别式掩码任务预训练的编码器虽然擅长语义对齐，但由于缺乏解码结构，其在向多模态生成式任务迁移时面临显著的架构鸿沟[43]。

随着跨模态融合的加深，模态表征间的冲突与博弈逐渐显现。研究证实，在统一架构中强行联合预训练多种高资源模态（如语音与文本）会遭遇显著的模态容量限制（Capacity Limitations），导致信号间的相互干扰，甚至引发特定模态下游性能的退化[18]。为突破这一网络瓶颈，多模态预训练引入了稀疏混合专家（MoE）路由机制。通过优化 top-k 路由策略并设计专家原型（Expert Prototyping）配合 top-1 路由，模型在训练阶段大幅增加了可用参数规模，同时在部署与推理阶段维持了恒定的计算成本。这一策略有效缓解了跨模态表征干扰，并在万亿级别参数的图文联合预训练中展现出了显著的收敛加速能力[15]。

除了模型架构限制，跨模态对齐效果还受制于多模态数据固有的物理特性。图像-文本对齐通常只需关注空间对象与词汇间的静态语义一致性，而涉及视频、音频等连续模态时，则需建立额外的时间维度与节奏对应机制[53]。进一步地，仅依赖静态视听数据集进行的对齐被证明难以实现模型对物理世界的真正理解。为弥合语言系统与真实物理环境间的认知鸿沟，研究指出通过引入具身多模态代理（Embodied Agents），将空间位置、手势姿态等动态情境变量叠加到多模态交互通道中，正成为推动模型跨越表层特征映射、实现深度实体接地（Grounded Understanding）与意图对齐的关键演进方向[11]。

sections.title: 跨模态表示与对齐
sections.body:
跨模态表示与对齐致力于打破独立模态的壁垒。早期的双流模型虽在检索上表现出色，但其对比学习目标容易引发依赖数据增强的采样偏差，且受限的文本编码器难以胜任多模态生成任务[36][44]。为克服这些局限，近期研究在统一架构与融合机制上衍生出多条演进路线。

在统一编码与掩码建模方面，为消除特定模态隔离，M3AE放弃了对比学习，在共享编码器上采用高文本掩码率（50%-90%）的联合掩码标记预测，有效利用了非成对数据[44]。VL-BEiT利用混合模态专家（MoE）Transformer，将掩码图像、掩码语言及跨模态掩码建模在单一主干上统一[51]。面对非对齐海量语料，UNIMO结合跨模态对比学习与文本重写生成的困难负样本来增强语义空间[7]；其演进版本UNIMO-2则构建了共享的视觉-语言基础空间，实现了非对齐图像和文本的端到端联合学习[49]。针对语言与视觉的扩展瓶颈，PaLI模型验证了编码器-解码器语言模型（mT5）与视觉大模型（ViT）联合缩放的可行性[45]。为降低计算负担，Dynamic MDETR在视觉定位解码器中采用2D自适应采样，仅使用少量特征点即可完成文本引导解码[35]；而LXMERT-S则提出基于词、短语到句子粒度的多阶段策略，以极小参数量逼近大模型性能[16]。

将跨模态对齐扩展至多语言环境带来了参数膨胀和语义偏差挑战。MULE采用单一共享语言分支替代独立特定语言模型，有效控制了规模[2]；SMALR进一步提出固定大小的语言无关表示及掩码跨语言建模损失，在极低参数下支持十余种语言[6]。为实现零样本跨语言迁移，UC2等模型通过机器翻译扩充数据，并构建以图像为枢纽的掩码区域建模与翻译建模任务[8][22]。然而机器翻译易丢失文化特征，KELIP通过真实韩英双语图文对和多裁剪增强，成功捕捉到跨语言同义词在视觉语义上的文化差异[40]。为降低语言扩展门槛，MLA框架向单语CLIP中注入轻量级语言获取模块，通过两阶段训练实现低成本扩展[37]。在语音领域，mSLAM将w2v-BERT与SpanBERT结合，通过对齐语音和转录文本的CTC损失，在多语种中建立了跨模态共享表示[58]。针对跨语言VQA，结合语言学先验损失与代码混合增强能显著缓解对源语言的过拟合[39]。

在信息注入与细粒度融合方面，部分研究侧重非破坏性的映射或前缀机制。VaLM通过检索相关图像并在视觉知识融合层中执行注意力计算，直接增强了自回归语言模型[54]；部分研究利用对象感知网络将图像转译为输入空间中的辅助文本序列，在不修改BERT架构的情况下实现了多模态情感分类[13]；另有工作将包含物理感觉运动规范的视觉基础词向量直接替换至ELECTRA等模型中以提供具身物理感知[12]。TEASEL利用语音提取的动态前缀作为预训练语言模型交叉注意力的输入[20]，而HVPNeT将对象级图像特征作为可插拔视觉前缀逐层引导文本，避免了无关图像的干扰[38]。解耦实验证实，模态间相互参考的多模态注意力在零样本检索中优于单模态独立注意力[10]。针对复杂的视频序列，VLM采用掩码模态模型强制网络利用另一模态恢复被遮盖模态，增强了跨模态表示紧密度[24]；VICTOR引入对比代理任务捕捉长视频特有的时空与序列关系[23]；DeCEMBERT则利用熵最小化约束注意力，迫使模型在噪声指令视频中自动聚焦对齐的字幕[9]。

sections.title: 训练数据和交互生成
sections.body:
多模态大语言模型在训练数据利用与交互生成机制上，已从单一范式演进为零样本模型组合与检索增强多模态预训练两大核心分支。

在交互生成方面，无需额外微调的零样本多模型组合机制成为扩展跨模态能力的重要路径。Socratic Models通过多模态提示（Multimodal-informed prompting）引导不同领域分布的预训练模型（如视觉语言模型和纯大语言模型）进行基于语言的零样本信息交换以实现联合推理[48]。然而，这种级联架构存在单向通信局限，后续处理的信息无法回传纠错。为此，迭代共识机制突破了该限制，引入闭环通信优化：由生成器构建初始候选方案，并由多个评分器组成的集成模块提供迭代反馈；这种闭环机制促使模型间相互修正误差，从而提升零样本任务的稳健性[32]。在交互指令形式的拓展上，VIMA架构将跨模态生成目标延伸至具身智能，其将复杂的任务规范统一表达为交织文本与视觉特征序列的多模态提示（Multimodal prompts），并在解码端通过Transformer自回归地输出连续运动控制动作[50]。

在训练数据与知识注入机制方面，为突破静态模型参数对世界知识存储的容量瓶颈，检索增强架构被实质性地引入多模态语言建模中。MuRAG构建了多模态检索增强Transformer，通过联合对比损失与生成损失（Joint contrastive and generative loss），在海量图文及纯文本混合语料上进行预训练，使生成过程能实时访问外部非参数化多模态记忆以完成复杂推理问答[42]。相比之下，RA-CM3进一步实现了检索内容与生成目标的模态对等化。该机制结合了CM3生成器架构与基于CLIP的检索器，不仅在训练时仅需极低的计算开销，更首次具备了检索并直接生成图文混合序列（Mixtures of text and images）的能力，同时解锁了多模态上下文学习的新特性[59]。

针对多模态表征融合的预训练框架层，i-Code超越了传统依赖成对视频数据的对齐范式，提出一种高灵活度的自监督学习机制。该系统前端复用独立预训练的单模态编码器，后端接入多模态融合网络，通过创新的掩码模态单元建模（Masked modality unit modeling）和跨模态对比学习目标进行端到端预训练，使得模型在推理阶段能够动态兼容单、双或三模态数据的任意输入组合[57]。

sections.title: 模态泛化、幻觉与边界
sections.body:
多模态大语言模型在跨模态泛化与生成质量控制上展现出明确的机制分化，其核心研究重点已从基础特征的对齐拼接，直接演进为统一语义空间的离散化映射边界及解码期的事实性约束。

在模态泛化机制的分支演进中，将非结构化、连续的多模态信号强制映射至离散的文本词元空间，已成为实现架构泛化的终局方案，有效规避了早期复杂的跨模态注意力融合设计。例如，MAnTiS方法通过模态特定编码器，将图像与文本直接投影至标准的文本词元空间并构建联合条件前缀；该机制直接引导预训练语言模型生成，无需复杂网络缝合即可实现单模态向多模态的条件生成泛化[17]。面对包含视频与音频的复杂连续流，VX2TEXT框架采用了更彻底的映射策略：引入可学习的连续输入松弛机制（Differentiable Tokenizer），将视频或语音转化为统一的语言嵌入。这种将多模态强制折叠进语言语义空间的操作，使得自回归解码器能够无缝接管多模态特征，彻底消除了针对字幕生成或问答定制专用网络头的需求，实现了判别与生成任务的统一泛化[25]。

然而，高度统一的词元化泛化机制直接暴露出多模态生成的边界——事实性偏移与多模态幻觉。当模型具备强生成自由度时，常输出与条件输入相悖或脱节的细节。针对此局限，干预解码过程成为了更具确定性的机制分支。XFBoost框架放弃对内部注意力权重的隐式干预，转而在解码阶段直接将提取的视觉语义属性注入为显式约束条件。配合策略梯度（Policy Gradient）技术进行强化微调，该机制在不损失生成多样性的前提下，精准压制了违背事实或特征矛盾的幻觉表达，大幅拉升了图文一致性边界[56]。

此外，多模态泛化的极限不仅受制于网络架构，更受到文化与先验分布的严格限制。即使在数据增广和表征解偏的加持下，模态知识的跨领域迁移依然存在物理与文化鸿沟。在多模态机器翻译中，利用预训练视觉语言模型（VLM）虽能缓解平行语料瓶颈，但其实验证据表明多模态对齐存在刚性的文化距离边界。当视觉融合机制应用于与预训练数据（如LXMERT）文化背景差异巨大的目标语言体系时，多模态特征带来的性能增益可能会发生衰退[46]。这表明，多模态大模型的泛化边界无法单靠底层词元映射来无限延伸，物理世界的分布差异构成了当前对齐机制的刚性壁垒。

sections.title: 实验证据与方法比较
sections.body:
多模态模型的评估正经历从单模态、高资源向多语言、多模态全景拓展的演进。为解决多模态任务多语言支持匮乏的问题，GEM基准整合了图像与视频维度的多语言评测，并引入M3P等架构作为统一对照[14]。然而，直接将机器翻译用于构建多语言集往往引入文本伪影，为此Crossmodal-3600要求双语者依据图像生成36种语言的原生描述，建立了规避翻译伪影的高质量参照系[33]。Bloom Library则进一步将基准覆盖面扩展至300多种语言，为极低资源语种确立了零样本评测基线[30]。在模态复杂度的扩展上，MUGEN基准利用强化学习智能体生成带有音频属性的闭世界受控视频，并设计了针对真实样本校准的人类评估协议[41]；CMU-MOSEAS构建了覆盖法语、德语、西班牙语和葡萄牙语的音视频基准，并利用F1分数评估不平衡类别下的多模态情感属性[5]。

为了准确剥离模型的统计拟合捷径，评估机制逐渐向引入严格去偏见对照条件的探针网络发展。传统测试常受语言共现偏置污染，近期的研究通过构建针对性探针来测试视觉概念的真实落地。例如，通过对齐结构以控制目标与干扰项的相互翻转，能有效排查纯语言先验，从而测试模型对谓词-名词的真实跨模态依赖[34]。此外，为消除巨型模型引入的控制变量困难，有研究通过构建“数学-语言”微型沙盒作为对照环境，以低算力开销验证了单流架构在融合机制中优于双流架构的特性，且该结论与视觉语言域的演进结论保持一致[31]。

在更精细的对照条件下，实验发掘出多模态预训练在能力边界和表征习得上的诸多冲突结果。首先，在零样本跨语言评估中，尽管引入架构适配，多模态模型仍会出现约38个准确率分数的骤降，暴露了深层潜在的跨语言多模态严重未对齐[27]。其次，关于模型视觉常识来源的探查得出了反直觉的结论：基于“记忆颜色”探针任务的对照显示，多模态模型表现出的视觉常识水平，纯单模态语言基线仅通过文本预训练即可达到同等水准，多模态预训练在此处并未展现显著增益[55]。在进一步严格过滤文本数据中视觉相关词汇后，纯语言模型依然能表现出部分视觉常识，这暗示模型机制上可能通过二阶同义词泄露来获取跨模态特征[21]。最后，针对颜色与尺寸的多模态探针实验明确证实，模型在处理空间位置和大小推断时仍严重依赖语言先验线索，且针对多模态下游任务的微调操作，并不必然能够改善模型底层的细粒度多模态表征能力[29]。

sections.title: 局限、效率与开放问题
sections.body:
现有多模态大语言模型在理论上追求跨模态信息的平衡整合，但在实际机制中却存在深层的对齐不对称问题。通过非侵入式的跨模态输入消融诊断发现，无论单流还是双流视觉-语言模型，均表现出“视觉辅助语言”而非真正对称的融合模式：完全或选择性地屏蔽视觉输入会大幅增加掩码文本预测的相对困难，而屏蔽文本输入对视觉对象类别（掩码图像区域）的预测几乎不产生任何负面影响[26]。这种现象违背了跨模态双向激活的预设假设。造成此种表征失效的部分原因在于，传统模型依赖外部视觉组件提取的噪声银标准目标分布缺乏可靠性，从而阻碍了语言特征反向指导视觉理解的通道[26]。这表明现有的跨模态架构尚未在深层语义网络中实现各模态地位的完全平等。

在模型向复杂真实世界部署的过程中，物理环境和数据传输产生的分布偏移构成了主要应用限制。针对视频-语言模型的评估显示，跨模态检索系统对于多模态扰动展现出明显的不平衡：模型对文本层面的扰动具有相对较强的鲁棒性，但对视觉层面的扰动（如光照剧变、相机移动或数字压缩）更为敏感且易发生性能退化[47]。在注意力机制分配上，模型倾向于将权重集中于静态场景和物理实体，而对时序运动与具体动作特征的捕捉存在系统性不足[47]。尽管采用预训练范式的模型在应对这些扰动时相较于从头训练的模型表现出更宽的鲁棒性边界，但核心的动作理解缺陷仍是目前视频与语言对齐的未决难题[47]。

针对上述跨模态特征的局限性，部分研究尝试在特定下游应用中引入强化机制。例如，在情感分析等需要细粒度模态交互的任务中，采用独立的自监督学习模型为各单一模态提取高层特征表示，并引入鲁棒的跨模态注意力网络进行融合集成，能够在不依赖严格时间对齐假设的情况下，有效捕捉长程依赖并克服低级特征表征能力薄弱的问题[19]。然而，从整体多模态范式来看，此类方法级别的补救尚未解决宏观验证条件的缺失。真实世界鲁棒性分析常因获取真实分布偏移数据的极高难度，不得不妥协于使用人工模拟噪声进行基准测试[47]。此外，多模态模型的训练和测试严重依赖庞大的GPU算力开销，且基准验证受制于重度预处理要求及模型权重的公开状态，这些工程与资源壁垒直接限制了模型评测的覆盖广度与开放问题的探索进度[47]。
